## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

Five juan (juan 9–13 of the comprehensive *Xiūzhēn shíshū* 修真十書), preserved in the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (DZ 0263b / CT 263b, juan 9–13 = TC 262 part 2), 洞真部 方法類. The author Xiāo Tíngzhī 蕭廷芝 (*zì* Yuánruì, *hào* Zǐxū liǎozhēnzǐ), a native of Fúzhōu 福州 (Fújiàn) and disciple of Péng Sì 彭耜 (one of [Bái Yùchán](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%99%BD%E7%8E%89%E8%9F%BE)'s most prominent followers), here assembles a wide-ranging compendium of Southern-lineage *nèidān* 內丹 thought that became a key reference work for the late Sòng and Yuán. The title-page calls Xiāo *Zǐxū Liǎozhēnzǐ Xiāo Tíngzhī Yuánruì shù* 紫虛了眞子蕭廷芝元瑞述. Juan 9 (= *Xiūzhēn shíshū* 9) opens with a *Wújí tú shuō* 無極圖說 — Xiāo's commentary on the *Tàijí tú* 太極圖 of Zhōu Dūnyí 周敦頤 in alchemical register — followed by diagrams illustrating the interaction of *qì* 氣 and *jīng* 精 in the *nèidān* process, their circulation, and the rules of fire-phasing (9.1a–7b), then three poems and a treatise on the cyclically transformed elixir. Juan 10 is wholly devoted to the *Jīndān wèndá* 金丹問答 ("Questions and Answers on the Elixir"), a lexicon of *nèidān* terms in *yǔlù* 語錄 (recorded conversations) form; it is also reproduced in *[DZ 570 Yǎngshēng bìlù](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0570)* 19a–32b and in the collection *Jīndān jíwén* 金丹集問 by Hú Wénhuàn 胡文煥 (fl. 1596) in *Gézhì cóngshū* 格致叢書. Juan 11 and 12 contain *nèidān*-themed regular and *cí* 詞 poetry; the *cí* of 12.7a–12b are reproduced (without attribution) in juan 7 and 8 of *[DZ 1100 Mínghè yúyīn](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c1100)*. Juan 13 contains a commentary on the *Cuīgōng rǔyào jīng* 崔公入藥鏡 (cf. *[DZ 135 Cuīgōng rǔyào jīng zhùjiě](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0135)*, where Xiāo's gloss is quoted extensively) and one on Lǚ Dòngbīn's 呂洞賓 *cí*-lyric *Qìnyuánchūn* 沁園春 (cf. *[DZ 136 Lǚ Chúnyáng zhēnrén Qìnyuánchūn dāncí zhùjiě](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0136)*).

**Abstract**

Farzeen Baldrian-Hussein, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:840 (§3.A.4, *Nèidān* and *Yǎngshēng*), establishes that Xiāo Tíngzhī was a disciple of Péng Sì 彭耜, one of Bái Yùchán's most famous followers — an attribution attested by Xiāo's preface dated 1260 to *[DZ 687 Dàodé zhēnjīng sānjiě](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0687)* (preface 8a). Another source (the *Quán Sòng cí* 全宋詞 4.2777) confirms that Xiāo bore two *zì*: Yuánruì 元瑞 and Tiānlái 天賴. The *Jīndān dàchéng jí* is quoted frequently in *[DZ 1005 Zhōuyì cāntóng qì fāhuī](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c1005)* (e.g., 3.3b, 5.18b, 6.2b); since the *Fāhuī* itself has a preface dated 1284, the second half of the thirteenth century is the latest possible date for the present collection. The frontmatter accordingly brackets composition 1255–1284, with Xiāo's *fl.* 1260 datable preface to *Dàodé sānjiě* providing a secure anchor in the middle of the bracket. The compilation captures the late-Southern-lineage *nèidān* synthesis in the generation after Bái Yùchán, integrating Zhōu Dūnyí's *Tàijí tú*, the Cuīgōng *rǔyào* lexicon, the *Cāntóng qì* fire-phasing tradition, and Lǚ Dòngbīn's lyric inheritance into a single anthology that was to remain influential through the Yuán and into the Míng.
